result.title: Accounting Policy Manual - posting authority, support, approvals
result.text:
HALVARD SYSTEMS - ACCOUNTING POLICY MANUAL (excerpt), effective 2026-01-01
Applies to Halvard Systems Inc. (US), Halvard Systems Ltd (UK), Halvard Systems GmbH (DE).

1. Posting authority. Senior accountants may post manual journal entries up to USD 10,000
   per entry (local-currency entries are measured at the month-end rate of the entry month).
   Any entry above USD 10,000 must be routed to the Controller with an approval request
   (request_approval) immediately after posting; it remains pending until approved.
   Splitting one transaction into several entries to stay under the threshold is prohibited.
2. Support. Every journal entry must have its supporting document(s) attached. An entry
   without support is not a valid entry.
3. Capitalization. Individual equipment purchases of USD 2,500 or more (local-currency
   equivalent at the month-end rate) are capitalized to 1500 Computer Equipment and
   depreciated over 36 months beginning the month after acquisition.
4. Prepaids. Payments covering services or events in future periods (more than one month
   out, or spanning more than one month) above USD 1,000 are recorded as prepaid (1210
   Prepaid Software for software, 1220 Prepaid Insurance for insurance, 1200 Prepaid Expenses
   for everything else, including deposits for future events) and expensed straight-line over
   the coverage period starting the month coverage begins, or when the event occurs.
5. Accruals. Expenses are recorded in the period the goods or services are received. Services
   received but not yet invoiced at month-end are accrued to 2100 Accrued Expenses using the
   best available evidence (vendor statements, approved timesheets, engagement terms).
   Quotes or proposals for future work are not liabilities.
6. Revenue. Revenue is recognized under ASC 606 per the contract terms. Deferred revenue
   (2200) is released as performance obligations are satisfied. Usage earned but not yet
   invoiced is recorded to 1300 Unbilled Receivables.
7. Customer credits. SLA credits are issued only per contract terms and verified uptime data
   (see the monthly uptime report). Credits are recorded as a reduction of the related revenue.
8. Cash application. Customer receipts are applied to invoices per remittance advice. Receipts
   that cannot be matched to an open invoice remain in 2950 Unapplied Cash.
9. FX. Monetary balances denominated in a currency other than the entity's functional
   currency are remeasured at the month-end rate; gains/losses go to 6950 FX Gain/Loss.
   Intercompany charges are recorded by the receiving entity at the month-end rate of the
   month charged.
10. Payroll. Returned payroll deposits are recorded to 2150 Accrued Payroll & Unclaimed
   Wages until reissued. Unpaid wages at month-end are accrued to 2150.
11. Exceptions. Items that cannot be supported must be reported via flag_exception. Never
   post an entry to force a reconciliation or to make balances agree.
12. Periods. January and February 2026 are closed. March 2026 is open.

MEMO - US March 2026 Close (assigned items)
To: Controller
From: David Murguia, Senior Accountant
Date: 2026-04-03
Re: US depreciation, prepaid software amortization, and Parker & Rowe legal accrual

SUMMARY
All three assigned US items for the March 2026 period are complete. Three journal entries were posted at 2026-03-31, each with supporting documentation attached. One entry exceeds my posting authority and has been routed to you for approval.

1) DEPRECIATION - JE-00304 - USD 3,425.00 (posted, within authority)
   Dr 6800 Depreciation 3,425.00 / Cr 1510 Accumulated Depreciation 3,425.00
   Support: DOC-0067 (Fixed asset register & depreciation schedule Q1 2026, US)
   Per the register, computer equipment (GL 1500) cost USD 164,400.00 is depreciated straight-line
   over 36 months = USD 3,425.00/month. No additions or disposals in Q1 2026 through 2026-03-31,
   so the March charge is unchanged from Jan/Feb. Jan and Feb were already booked; March was not.
   Roll-forward check: opening accumulated depreciation at 2026-01-01 of USD 41,100.00 + three
   months at 3,425.00 (10,275.00) = USD 51,375.00, which agrees exactly to the post-entry GL
   balance in 1510. Account 6800 YTD is now USD 10,275.00.

2) PREPAID SOFTWARE AMORTIZATION - JE-00305 - USD 1,250.00 (posted, within authority)
   Dr 6200 Software Subscriptions 1,250.00 / Cr 1210 Prepaid Software 1,250.00
   Support: DOC-0068 (Prepaid software amortization schedule 2026, US)
   Figtree Platform annual license, invoice FIG-20260105, USD 15,000.00, term 2026-01-01 to
   2026-12-31, straight-line = USD 1,250.00/month. Jan and Feb booked; March was not.
   Roll-forward check: 15,000.00 less three months (3,750.00) = USD 11,250.00 remaining prepaid,
   which agrees exactly to the post-entry GL balance in 1210 (9 months of coverage remaining).

3) MARCH LEGAL FEE ACCRUAL - JE-00306 - USD 14,250.00 (posted, PENDING YOUR APPROVAL)
   Dr 6500 Legal Fees 14,250.00 / Cr 2100 Accrued Expenses 14,250.00
   Support: DOC-0206 (Parker & Rowe LLP billing email dated 2026-04-01)
   Counsel confirmed time recorded on Halvard Systems Inc. matters through 2026-03-31 totals
   USD 14,250.00 (Series B side-letter review), with their invoice to issue in April. This is
   services received but not yet invoiced at month-end, accrued on best available evidence per
   Policy 5 (DOC-0005). This is a vendor statement of time actually recorded, not a quote or
   proposal for future work, so it is a proper liability at 3/31.

APPROVAL POLICY
Per Policy 1 (DOC-0005), senior accountants may post up to USD 10,000 per entry. JE-00306 at
USD 14,250.00 exceeds that limit, so I submitted an approval request immediately after posting;
it is currently in pending_approval status and requires your sign-off to be final. JE-00304 and
JE-00305 are below the threshold and required no approval. I did not split the legal accrual to
stay under the limit, which Policy 1 prohibits.

CONTROLS / DUPLICATE CHECK
Before posting I confirmed March activity in 6800, 1510, 6200, 1210 and 6500 was all zero, so
there is no double-booking of the schedule-driven entries. I also searched the ledger for any
existing Parker & Rowe activity in the US entity and found none, confirming the accrual is not a
duplicate of a booked invoice.

JUDGMENT ITEM FOR YOUR AWARENESS (no action taken)
The Parker & Rowe fees are described as "Series B side-letter review." Legal costs that are
direct incremental costs of issuing equity are normally charged against additional paid-in
capital (3100) rather than expensed. I found no supporting documentation of an equity issuance
in March 2026 and the work is described as a side-letter review of an existing arrangement, so
I recorded the full amount to 6500 Legal Fees consistent with my assignment. If you are aware of
an in-flight Series B closing, please let me know and I will reclassify all or part of the
USD 14,250.00 to APIC before the books are finalized.

CHECKLIST STATUS
- US "Record depreciation": marked complete.
- US "Amortize prepaid software": marked complete.
- The legal accrual is not a standalone checklist line; it falls under AP cutoff/accruals, which I
  have left open as it covers scope beyond my assigned items.
Other open US items (bank reconciliations, unpaid payroll accrual, AP cutoff review,
intercompany reconciliation, revenue recognition, flux review) were outside this assignment and
remain open.

EXCEPTIONS
None. All three items were fully supported, so no flag_exception was raised and no entry was
posted to force a reconciliation.

Net P&L impact of the above: USD 18,925.00 of additional March expense (3,425.00 depreciation,
1,250.00 software amortization, 14,250.00 legal), of which 14,250.00 is subject to your approval.
